title: Tetzaveh: Moses' name is missing
hook: Moses isn't named in this portion; some link it to his offer to be blotted out for his people (Exodus 32:32)

segments.voice: Yesterday, the ner tamid, the lamp that burns continually, fed with oil from crushed olives. Your line was crushed olives give light. Today, still in Tetzaveh, something that isn't there.

Look closely at the credits of a big movie and you'll find hundreds of names. But the person who stayed up all night fixing the sound in one scene might not be there. The neighbor who watched the director's kids for a year definitely isn't. Since the night he was born in Egypt, Moses has been in almost every scene of the Torah: Pharaoh, the bush, the plagues, the sea, Sinai. Then comes this portion, Tetzaveh. Read it start to finish, and his name isn't in it once.
screen: `THE NAMES IN THE CREDITS.` → `THE ONES WHO AREN'T THERE.` → `TETZAVEH: NO MOSES.`

segments.voice: People who read the Torah closely have long pointed this out. From his birth in Exodus to the end of Numbers, Tetzaveh is said to be the one weekly portion where the name Moses never appears. He isn't absent, though. The portion opens, in Hebrew, v'atah tetzaveh: and you, you shall command. God is speaking to Moses the whole time. Make the oil. Dress Aaron. Ordain the priests. Moses is the you on every line, everywhere and unnamed. Why? The Torah doesn't say. A medieval commentator, the Baal HaTurim, looks ahead a few chapters, to the golden calf. After the people sin, Moses pleads for them, and says to God, in the old Jewish translation: "blot me, I pray Thee, out of Thy book which Thou hast written." Forgive them, or take my name out. The Baal HaTurim says the words of a righteous person carry weight even when said conditionally, and so his name was left out of one portion. Others notice that this portion is all about Aaron, his brother: Aaron's clothes, Aaron's sons, Aaron's role. Perhaps Moses steps back so his brother can stand in the light. Neither answer is in the text itself, but both point the same way. The greatest prophet in the Torah spends a whole portion as the unnamed you, doing the work, giving instructions that make someone else shine.
screen: `A PORTION WITHOUT HIS NAME.` · `V'ATAH: AND YOU, ON EVERY LINE.` · `BLOT ME OUT OF THY BOOK.` · `STEPPING BACK FOR AARON.` · then, large: `STEP OUT OF THE FRAME.`

segments.voice: Think of something kind you could do where no one would know it was you: paying for someone's coffee, praising a colleague to their boss out of their hearing, giving anonymously. Picture doing it and walking away without a word. If part of you wants credit, that's normal; let it be there, and stay with the picture anyway.
Tetzaveh. You shall command. The portion where Moses is the you on every line, and his name never appears.
Your line: step out of the frame. His name can wait, and the work goes on. See you tomorrow.

howItsDone: Jewish teachers often point out Moses' missing name when Tetzaveh is read; tradition also places Moses' death on the seventh of Adar, which often falls near this portion. Jewish law ranks giving anonymously among the highest forms of tzedakah.
